# Trump’s approval ratings endure a cruel summer

President Trump is enduring a difficult summer in public opinion polls, with his falling approval rating deepening concerns for Republicans that they could lose the House and Senate majorities this fall.

Trump has hit record lows in various polls, including a 33 percent approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll this week. [...] In the latest Economist/YouGov survey, Trump is exiting August with a 33 percent approval rating, a new low for him in that poll.

Trump’s polling in the Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) average did see a slight increase Thursday, reaching 39.2 percent.

results.title: Trump’s approval ratings endure a cruel summer

results.content:
A Reuters/Ipsos poll released Aug. 31 found that 33% of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, marking the third consecutive week at that level.

The 33% rating was Trump’s lowest in Reuters/Ipsos polling since he returned to the White House in 2025. It also matched his lowest approval rating during his first term, which came in December 2017.

The latest national figure was also below former President Joe Biden’s lowest approval rating, which reached 35% in October 2024. [...] The New York Times averages several other polls daily. Its data says Trump stands at 58% disapproval and 38% approval as of Sept. 1.
 Silver Bulletin's poll shows 58% disapprove and 38.2% approve as of Sept. 1

The poll, released on Sunday, Sept. 6, found that only 32% of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, a three-point drop from last month’s edition and the lowest the president has seen in Focaldata/Financial Times tracking since it began in May.
